title: Agent Builder's Playbook — Oct 2, 2026
intro: Cost and evaluation lead this edition: route models per task, and eval the whole agent configuration.

cards.title: Route each coding task to the cheapest model that can handle it
cards.problem: Sending every agent step to your top model inflates cost on tasks a cheaper model handles fine.
cards.apply: Add a model router inside the agent harness that picks the model per task, as Open SWE does, and compare router output against your single-model baseline on your own task set before switching traffic.
cards.result: LangChain reports a 64% cut in median cost per coding task with no measurable quality drop.

evidence.note: LangChain reports a 64% median cost reduction on Open SWE coding tasks with no measurable quality drop.

cards.title: Hillclimb against evals only after you have checked the graders
cards.problem: Optimizing prompts against an unvalidated eval rewards graders' blind spots, not real quality.
cards.apply: Build the eval, verify each grader against hand-labeled cases first, then iterate on the app. The claude-api skill's build-eval and hillclimb commands automate this loop.
cards.result: Score gains you see are more likely to reflect real improvement rather than overfit grading.

evidence.note: Editorial inference from Anthropic's published principles for designing evals and hillclimbing without fooling yourself.

cards.title: Package agent permissions as an OCI artifact alongside the agent
cards.problem: Agent access rules live in ad-hoc configs, so they drift between laptop, CI and cloud.
cards.apply: Describe filesystem, network and tool access in a Docker Sandbox Kit spec and ship it with the agent image, so every environment enforces the same declared permissions.
cards.result: The same agent runs with identical, reviewable access boundaries wherever it is deployed.

evidence.note: Editorial inference from Docker's announcement donating the Sandbox Kit Specification to the CNCF.

cards.title: Snapshot GPU pods to cut model cold-start time
cards.problem: Autoscaled inference pods spend minutes loading large model weights before serving a request.
cards.apply: On GKE, enable Pod Snapshots so CPU and GPU memory is checkpointed to Cloud Storage and restored on scale-up, and budget for managing snapshot lifecycle.
cards.result: Google's benchmarks report up to 89% lower startup latency, with a 70B model loading in 37 seconds.

evidence.note: Google's published GKE Pod Snapshot benchmarks report up to 89% lower startup latency and a 37-second 70B load.

cards.title: Evaluate the agent configuration, not just the model
cards.problem: Single success-rate numbers hide that cost, consistency and robustness shift with the agent's configuration.
cards.apply: Treat prompts, tools and harness settings as variables in your eval matrix, and report cost, consistency and robustness for each configuration alongside success rate.
cards.result: You can see which configuration change moved the metric before shipping it.

evidence.note: Editorial inference from the paper's argument that agents are configurable systems, not fixed models.

cards.title: Version, test and ship agent context like code
cards.problem: Prompts, rules and context files change by hand with no tests, review or rollback.
cards.apply: Keep context in a repo, add evals that run in CI on every change, and distribute it through a package manager with observability on what the agent actually loaded.
cards.result: Context regressions are caught in CI and are traceable to a specific commit.

evidence.note: Editorial inference from Patrick Debois's talk on treating context with testing, CI/CD and package management.
